why: We want AI to save staff time on planning and paperwork. We must protect kids' information and keep the trust of families, the district and our funders.
who_it_covers: Staff, group leaders, volunteers, contractors including our grant writer, and board members.

tools.name: None yet
tools.approved_for: No AI tool is approved yet. Whether to approve ChatGPT or Gemini is a board question.

new_tools: Renee approves any new tool, add-on, plugin, agent or AI feature in software we have. Joy checks settings, and the district must agree if student data is involved.
accounts: Use a work account, not a personal one, and Joy checks that vendor training on what you type is turned off.
allowed_uses: Once a tool is approved, these are fine without asking, with no child information:
Activity plans, STEM projects and games for your group.
Drafting the weekly parent newsletter and translating it into Spanish and Vietnamese.

needs_approval.use: Any new AI tool, add-on, plugin or feature
Any AI use with student data
AI help on state grant reports

protected_information: Kids' names, photos and video; grades and test scores; attendance; IEP and 504 information; allergies and medications; custody and pickup details; incident reports; the donor list; passwords and logins.
off_limits: Never use AI for mandated reporting. If you suspect abuse, call it in.
No AI-made images of our kids, and no AI-edited photos of real kids.
Never paste a child's information into AI. Our district agreement keeps student records in the platform.
check_before_it_goes_out: Read all AI output before it goes out. Check pickup times, dates, names and numbers.
Check outcomes numbers in state grant reports against our own records.
You are responsible for anything you send, even if AI wrote it.
decisions_about_people: AI never decides who gets a place, an accommodation, or a consequence for a child.
AI may help plan general activities. It does not judge or write about one child.
being_open: Label translated newsletters as machine-translated, so parents know to ask if something looks wrong.
We tell parents before kids use AI chatbots in our program.
if_something_goes_wrong: Tell your site director the same day. Site directors tell Renee the same day.
Reporting a mistake is expected. No one is punished for telling us.
who_owns_this: Renee, executive director, owns this policy. Joy checks tool settings.
Renee shares it with staff and group leaders.
open_questions: Do we approve ChatGPT or Gemini for staff, and may group leaders use personal accounts?
Do kids get to use AI in homework hour, and do we follow each school's rule or make our own? (Board and principals)
Who checks the Vietnamese translation? Today only a parent volunteer checks the Spanish.
Do we tell funders, like the state, when AI helped with reports? Does the board approve this policy and later changes?
